LENS: DOES A NUMBER ON SCREEN MEAN WHAT IT SAYS.
This console has repeatedly shipped a number whose label was wrong: a fetch cap displayed as a count, a
ratio computed with a floored denominator, a fixture presented as live, a status word for three different
outcomes. Cross-check EVERY prominent number and status word on the live console against another surface
that should agree, or against the API response that produced it. Read /api/v1/* responses directly in the
signed-in browser context and compare to what is rendered. Hunt for: a count that is really a page size; a
percentage with an unstated denominator; two views disagreeing; a label that names a different population
than the number measures; a badge that never changes.

findings.claim: The console reports the verifier's deviation count two different ways on two live views — #actions says 1 deviation, #grounding says 24 — with no qualifier distinguishing the populations, because one counts action_manifest rows and the other counts action_verdict rows over a content-addressed action_id that repeats across incidents.
findings.where: #actions header caption (`.sec` line rendered at index.html:9610) vs #grounding verdict-distribution card + hero (grndRender, index.html:5544-5563). Signed-in as operator:kyriakosp, 1600x1000, both captured in ONE session at 2026-07-29T19:06:18Z.
findings.evidence:
Same session, same posture bar (CHAIN OK 6214, SSE LIVE):
• #actions rendered text: "50 of 113 · 52 verified · 1 deviation"  (screenshot <scratchpad>)
• #grounding rendered text: "67 match · 7 partial · 24 deviation" and "computed from 98 verdicts and 321 scored predictions, never asserted."  (screenshot .../atk/final_grounding.png)
• APIs read in the same browser context: GET /api/v1/actions?limit=1 -> counts {total:113, verified:52, deviations:1}; GET /api/v1/grounding -> verdicts {match:67, partial:7, deviation:24}, verdict_total:98.
• Full manifest population (GET /api/v1/actions?limit=5000 -> 113 rows, server caps at 200 but total is 113): verdict distribution over ALL manifests = match 48, partial 3, deviation 1, none 61. So the 24 deviation verdicts collapse onto exactly 1 manifest row.
• Server-side cause: core/db/action_manifest_read.go:127-131 `count(*) FILTER (WHERE verdict='deviation') FROM action_manifest` vs core/db/grounding_read.go:30 `SELECT verdict, count(*) FROM action_verdict GROUP BY 1`.
• Raw captures: .../atk/kx_final.json, .../atk/raw__api_v1_actions_limit_5000.json
• Not covered by e2e/surface-contradictions.mjs: it drives synthetic fixtures through ONE view at a time and only asserts within-view agreement (grep 'check(' — 22 assertions, none compares #actions counts to #grounding counts).
findings.consequence: #actions is the surface an operator reads to decide whether an op-class is safe to graduate to unattended AUTO, and it under-reports the clamping event ('a deviation … can never run unattended again') by 24x, so a widen-autonomy decision is taken from a number that says the fleet has one clamped action when the verifier recorded twenty-four.

findings.claim: The login gate reports EVERY non-429 failure — including a 404/5xx from a down or mis-routed control plane — as "unauthenticated — check the operator name and token", so a backend outage is presented to the operator as a bad password.
findings.where: Login gate (#agErr) on https://territory-grounder.example.net/ before #appRoot is revealed; source deploy/console/v2/index.html:7742-7743 (`if(r.status===429){…} if(!r.ok){ agErr("unauthenticated — check the operator name and token"); }`). 1280x900.
findings.evidence:

• Network trace from the signing-in page: GET /api/v1/whoami -> 401 (expected, unauthenticated), POST /api/v1/session -> **404**.
• Rendered #agErr textContent: "unauthenticated — check the operator name and token"; #appRoot still hidden=true. Screenshot: <scratchpad>

• Not covered: e2e/detail-error-copy.mjs applies exactly this discipline (cause named per status, advice that works) but only to the workflow-DETAIL 403/404/500 cases; e2e/tracer.mjs only asserts the gate renders on a 401. No oracle drives a non-401 status through the auth gate.
findings.consequence: During the exact minutes the governance console is unreachable — the console that owns the KILL switch and the approval queue — it tells the operator their credentials are wrong, sending them to re-type a password and chase LDAP instead of paging the control plane.

findings.where: #knowledge — header caption (knowRender), the "Operational rules" group in .know-index, and the .know-page detail pane (knowRulePage, index.html:5774-5778). Rail badge [data-badge="knowledge"]. 1600x1000, signed in.

result.coverage_note:
Method: Playwright (node .mjs, scripts in <scratchpad>) against the LIVE https://territory-grounder.example.net/ only, signed in via the real LDAP gate as operator:kyriakosp; every /api/v1/* read was issued from inside the authenticated browser context with credentials:include. Read-only throughout: no KILL, no approve/deny, no vote, no seal-secret submit; the only POST was the console's own login.

WHAT I EXERCISED. Enumerated all 22 views and all 18 [data-badge] values, then cross-checked every prominent number against the API that produced it and against a second rendering surface: alerts 2011/2020 (vs counts.total and the 50-row page), logs 8200-8230 (= ledger seq + alerts total), estate 367/371, estatedepth 10, knowledge 420-425, wiki 611/612 (= lesson_total 608 + 3 runbooks), skills 7, credentials 4, regime 0, grounding 68%, policy Semi-auto, awaiting 16-18, the header annunciator, the #grounding scorecard in full, #actions counts, #command's "showing 50 of 1521 recorded", #estate tiles, #estatedepth list header, #knowledge page count. Also probed page-size behaviour by requesting limit=5000 on alerts/sessions/ledger/actions (server caps at 200; actions' true population is 113 so that one is complete).

WHAT I REFUTED AND DROPPED (each looked like a finding first).
1. "Estate Depth 10 is a page-size artifact" — the badge derives node health from the limit=50 alerts page, and a 200-alert window yields 13 not-ok hosts instead of 10. But the 3 extra hosts (notrf01dmz01/02/03) are NOT in the estate graph at all, so the rendered number is currently correct. It is fragile, not wrong; I could not produce a live wrong value, so it is not reported.
2. "#grounding autonomy bands say 508 resolved unattended / 912 held while only 113 actions were ever sealed" — the bands count sessions (session_risk_audit, latest per external_ref) and every classified session in my 200-row sample carried an action_id, so the session-level reading is defensible under content-addressed action ids. Dropped as over-claiming. The related weaker observation I did NOT promote to a finding: the header annunciator prints AUTO 508 / NOTICE 102 / PAUSE 914 with no title, no aria-label and no window qualifier, sitting between "SSE LIVE" and a live clock, while the rail badge for the queue that actually needs a human reads 17.
3. #grounding's internal arithmetic all reconciles: match_rate 0.6837 = 67/98, signal_ratio 1.7432 = 0.4019/0.2305, precision/recall/FP-per-prediction all match the payload, verdicts sum to verdict_total.

WHAT I COULD NOT REACH. (a) The estate was healthy and quiet during the window — I never saw a POLL_PAUSE decision arrive, so the approvals strip, the vote path and any actuation-time number went unmeasured (and are off-limits read-only anyway). (b) #signals, #models, #modules and #workflows all showed "—" badges with no live read surface, so I could not cross-check anything there. (c) Everything beyond a 200-row server cap (1523 sessions, 2020 alerts, 8230 ledger+alert rows) is unverifiable from the console — I checked the captions that state those denominators, not the totals themselves. (d) The live control plane went 502 and then 404-on-POST /api/v1/session twice during the session (a sibling agent is actively deploying to this host), which cost roughly 20 minutes and is why finding 2's evidence exists; I re-verified findings 1, 3 and 4 in a single post-recovery session so they cannot be blamed on a mid-deploy state. (e) I did not re-run the 19 existing oracles; my "not covered by X" claims come from reading their assertions, not from executing them.

LENS: WHAT AN ASSISTIVE-TECH OPERATOR ACTUALLY EXPERIENCES, LIVE.
Use Chrome's own accessibility engine (CDP Accessibility.getFullAXTree / getPartialAXTree with
name.sources) — NOT innerText, which is blind to aria-hidden and to computed names. Walk the live console
as a keyboard+screen-reader user would: Tab through every view in order, activate things, read what the AX
tree says at each step. Hunt for: a control whose accessible name is empty, duplicated across many
elements, or misleading; a live region that announces the wrong thing or nothing when state changes; a
table whose header association is wrong so cells are announced under the wrong column; a focus order that
jumps around the page; a modal that does not trap focus; a state change conveyed only visually.

findings.claim: The live data-adoption loop calls the whole-view router (liveAdopt → revealConsole → route(view)), which rebuilds #view with no focus preservation, so a keyboard/screen-reader operator's focus is moved to <body> every ~10–25 seconds with NO user input at all, on every view — including #workflows, whose wfPreserveFocus() fix (certified green by e2e/workflows-focus.mjs) is bypassed entirely on the live path.
findings.where: LIVE https://territory-grounder.example.net/ , authenticated, 1440x900, Chromium. Views measured: #workflows (.wf-list [role=option]), #estatedepth (.e2-lrow), #modules (.mods-row). Root cause seen at live bundle index.html:4114 (`wfOnSelect` → `route("workflows")`), :8726/:8746 (SSE snapshot → route), and the periodic liveAdopt path.
findings.evidence:
Instrumented `window.route` wrapper on the live page (script <scratchpad>). Captured call with stack:
  view=workflows focusBefore="run:librenms-dc1-181929" focusAfter="BODY"
    at revealConsole (https://territory-grounder.example.net/:10725:9)
    at liveAdopt (…:7868:3)
    at async liveAdopt (…:10376:48)
No-input timeline (r12_wf.mjs): focus a run row, touch nothing → t=5s focus=run:librenms-dc1-181929, t=10s BODY, and BODY at 15/20/25/30/35s.
Generalised (r14_general.mjs): #estatedepth focus on .e2-lrow "■dc1reactive01vm" survives 5/10/15s then BODY at 20s, with the instrumented route() logging before="A.e2-lrow::■dc1reactive01vm" after="BODY"; #modules focus on .mods-row "crowdsec" survives to 20s then BODY at 25s, route() before="DIV.mods-row::crowdsec…" after="BODY".
User-provoked variant (r12_wf.mjs): Enter on a run row → focus preserved at t=0 ("run:librenms-dc1-181925") then BODY from t=60ms onward, 2/2 rows tested.
Why the oracle stays green: on the live console `wfIsLive()` returns **true** (measured: {"isLive":true,"runs":50}); e2e/workflows-focus.mjs runs against a static file server with no API, so wfRunsSrc is null, wfIsLive() is false, the `wfOnSelect` → route() branch at index.html:4114 never executes, and the oracle only ever drives wfRenderList/wfRenderMain, which do preserve focus.
findings.consequence: A screen-reader or keyboard operator inspecting a governed run, an estate node, or a connector module is thrown to <body> — losing the reading cursor and the Tab position — roughly every 10–25 seconds without doing anything, so reading a proposal before approving or denying it becomes an unwinnable race against the refresh timer.

findings.claim: Activating any of the 39 filter chips destroys the chip the operator just pressed (route() does `#facets.innerHTML=""` then rebuilds), dropping focus to <body>, and the resulting content change — up to a 97% collapse of the view — is announced in no live region.
findings.where: LIVE console, authenticated, 1440x900. `#facets .facet` buttons on 10 views (command, actions, workflows, signals, estatedepth, models, modules, secrets, skills, wiki). Live bundle index.html:3083 `const fb=$("#facets"); fb.innerHTML="";` and :3090 `onclick:()=>{facetState[name]=k;route(name);}`.
findings.evidence:
Full enumeration (script r06_facetproof.mjs, output facetproof.json): TOTALS {"chips":39,"viewsWithChips":10,"lostFocus":27,"announced":0,"contentChanged":24} over 29 keyboard activations (Enter on a focused chip). 27/29 landed on BODY (the other 2 were an auth-gate reload flake, re-tested clean below). 0/29 produced any live-region text.
Per-chip examples (view / chip / #view innerText length before→after / focus after / #tgAnnounce after):
  actions  "Deviations"      8813→246   BODY  ""
  actions  "Floored"         8813→246   BODY  ""
  workflows "Live"           4996→56    BODY  ""
  estatedepth "Crit"         6008→1319  BODY  ""
  command  "Deviations"      3802→229   BODY  ""
Clean re-measure (r15_final.mjs): actions/"Deviations" focused=true → active=BODY, ann=""; estatedepth/"Crit" → BODY, ann=""; secrets/"Missing" → BODY, ann="".
Cross-check (r11_contrast.mjs): on #actions the "Deviations" chip took the ribbon list from 50 rendered rows to 0 and #view text 8813→246 chars, while the ONLY live-region text on the page was the stale, unrelated "Run tg-liveness-… selected …" string left over from a previous #workflows interaction — i.e. a screen reader would still be holding the wrong message.
Not covered by the suite: e2e/aria-state.mjs only reads `aria-pressed` attributes; e2e/surface-contradictions.mjs sets `facetState.command = k` directly and calls the view function, bypassing the click → route() path; no oracle presses a chip and reads document.activeElement or #tgAnnounce.
findings.consequence: An operator filtering to "Deviations" or "Floored" — the exact triage move before approving or denying an actuation — is silently returned to the top of the page with no confirmation that the filter applied or that it left zero matching proposals, so "nothing to review" and "my keypress did nothing" are indistinguishable.

findings.claim: The #estatedepth node list is 217 tab stops in which the selected node is published only as a CSS class — 0/217 rows carry aria-current or aria-selected and the list container has no role or name — and activating a row calls draw() → list.replaceChildren(), destroying the focused anchor so focus lands on <body> and the next Tab restarts at row 0.
findings.where: LIVE console, #estatedepth, `#view .e2-list > a.e2-lrow` (href="#"). Live bundle index.html:5432–5438.
findings.evidence:
Census (r09_depth.mjs / depth.json): {"rows":217,"sel":1,"anyAriaCurrent":0,"anyAriaSelected":0,"listRole":null,"hrefs":["#"],"tabbable":217}. Selected row's full attribute list (r15_final.mjs): `class=e2-lrow sel href=#` — the ONLY difference from an unselected row is the `sel` class.
Activation, 5/5 rows tested (idx 3, 7, 12, 40, 100): after Enter, active="BODY", #tgAnnounce="" every time, while the inspector pane content did change (e.g. detail went to "dc1linkwarden02 / NLLEI01 / LXC / CRIT"). nextTab landed on `a.e2-lrow :: ■dc1cloudbeaver01lxc` — row 0 — in all 5 cases.
Tab cost measured directly (r10_tabcost.mjs): 34 Tabs from page start to node row 0; walked to row 5; Enter → focus=BODY; then **7 Tabs** to reach row 6 (i.e. focus restarted at row 0). Walking the estate node-by-node is therefore ~sum(1..217) ≈ 23,600 Tab presses instead of 217.

REFUTED AS STATED — the surface symptom is real, but the claim's "because" clause and its decisive evidence line are both factually false, and the claim is internally self-contradictory.

WHAT I REPRODUCED (independent session, live https://territory-grounder.example.net/, operator:kyriakosp, 1600x1000, 2026-07-29T19:09:12Z, posture CHAIN OK 6218 / SSE LIVE):
• #actions `.sec` caption, rendered text, exact: "50 of 113 · 52 verified · 1 deviation" (screenshot <scratchpad>)

• GET /api/v1/actions?limit=1 -> counts {total:113, verified:52, deviations:1}; GET /api/v1/grounding -> verdicts {match:67, partial:7, deviation:24}, verdict_total:98.
So the 1-vs-24 contradiction on the two live views is genuine. It is also NOT a !736 fix: `git diff da38c1f7..main` touches neither core/db/action_manifest_read.go nor core/db/grounding_read.go, and the undeployed index.html diff contains zero "deviation" lines.

WHY THE CLAIM STILL FAILS. The claim asserts the split arises "over a content-addressed action_id that repeats across incidents", and offers as its decisive evidence: "the 24 deviation verdicts collapse onto exactly 1 manifest row." I measured both directly against the live DB (read-only psql):
• `SELECT count(*), count(DISTINCT action_id) FROM action_verdict` -> 98 | 98
• `SELECT verdict, count(*), count(DISTINCT action_id) FROM action_verdict GROUP BY 1` -> match 67|67, partial 7|7, deviation 24|24
• `SELECT count(*), count(DISTINCT action_id) FROM action_manifest` -> 113 | 113
• deviation rows: 24 rows, 24 distinct action_id, 24 distinct plan_hash, across 16 distinct target hosts.
There is NO content-addressed repetition anywhere in either table — every id is 1:1. And the 24 deviations do not collapse onto one manifest row: a LEFT JOIN shows all 24 deviating action_ids DO have their own distinct manifest row (`SELECT v.verdict, count(*), count(m.action_id) FROM action_verdict v LEFT JOIN action_manifest m USING(action_id) GROUP BY 1` -> deviation 24|24). The stated cause is refuted.

THE CLAIM ALSO CONTRADICTS ITSELF. If the reporter's own mechanism were true — 24 verdicts collapsing onto 1 action — then exactly ONE distinct action was clamped, "#actions: 1 deviation" would be the CORRECT clamp count, and #grounding's 24 would be the misleading surface. The offered evidence, taken at face value, refutes the offered consequence ("under-reports the clamping event by 24x"). A finding whose evidence disproves its own conclusion cannot be accepted as stated.

THE ACTUAL MECHANISM (different, and it matters for the fix). Cross-tab of authoritative verdict vs the manifest's denormalized column:
  deviation -> manifest NULL: 23 ; deviation -> deviation: 1
  match     -> manifest NULL: 19 ; match     -> match:     48
  partial   -> manifest NULL:  4 ; partial   -> partial:    3
Both surfaces read the SAME population — there are no "two populations" to distinguish with a qualifier. action_manifest.verdict is simply never written back for 46 of the 98 verdicted actions (48+3+1 = 52 = the "52 verified" figure; 98-52 = 46 missing). So the defect is a stale/unwritten denormalized column, not a counting-population difference.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PARENT AGENT: do not discard the symptom — the underlying issue is real and more severe than described (23 of 24 genuinely distinct clamped actions, spanning 16 hosts, are invisible to #actions). But the remedy the claim implies — "add a qualifier distinguishing the populations" — is the wrong fix and would paper over a data-integrity bug; the correct fix is to repair the verdict writeback or derive the #actions count from action_verdict. The finding must be re-filed with the correct mechanism and evidence before it can be acted on.

   This is decisive because the claim's own exposure premise is the one that defeats it: the argument for the switch being announced is "Chrome exposes it as a live, unpruned child of the row button". (2) Captured a clean all-view baseline (out-BASE.json) to diff against. (3) Per-endpoint HTTP 500, one at a time, for /v1/estate, /v1/ledger, /v1/governance, /v1/sessions, /v1/actions, /v1/alerts, /v1/decisions, /v1/regime, and a total-starvation run covering all 22 views (out-STARVE.json). Rail badges correctly showed "—" under starvation. No retry storm on any endpoint under 500 or hang (request count stayed flat at 4 over 154s). No live API shape skew today — every key the console reads is present in the real response.

GAPS I DID NOT CLOSE. (a) I read in source that `page.decisions||[]`, `p.refs||[]`, `p.classes||[]` etc. would turn an HTTP 200 whose JSON parses but lacks the expected key into a confident empty ("No decisions awaiting a vote — Nothing is paused for a human"), because `catch` cannot see it. I did NOT drive that live, so I am not reporting it as a finding. (b) I did not fault-inject the SSE lanes (/v1/events, /v1/sessions/{ref}/stream). (c) I did not systematically test 403-vs-500 divergence per endpoint, nor malformed/empty-body per endpoint — I used 500 and starvation as the representative non-2xx and covered malformed/empty only on /v1/grounding. (d) I did not re-test the workflows detail-403 storm, since detail-403-no-storm.mjs already owns it. (e) Two runs were lost to a genuine mid-session outage (POST /api/v1/session returned 404 for ~2 minutes, confirmed by curl, unrelated to my interception); the grounding finding was re-verified afterwards on the current image, and login flakiness forced a retry loop in my harness. (f) I confirmed no existing oracle stalls a data endpoint mid-adopt-chain (only whoami in deeplink-every-view.mjs and logout in session-boundary.mjs) and none asserts on #command's .tile elements, but I did not execute the 19-oracle suite to prove it stays green against these defects.

result.why:
I tried to refute this four ways and it survived all of them. The finding stands as stated.

**1. The served bundle really does contain the defect (independent fetch).**
`curl https://territory-grounder.example.net/` → 200, 896,601 bytes, `last-modified: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 18:44:11 GMT` (fetched 19:21:51 GMT). At byte offset 696757 the currently-served `liveLogin` is verbatim:
```
if(r.status===429){ agBusy(false); agSpine("err"); agErr("rate limited — wait a minute and retry"); return; }
if(!r.ok){ agBusy(false); agSpine("err"); agErr("unauthenticated — check the operator name and token"); return; }
```
429 is the only status-specific branch. `grep -o '.\{300\}429.\{300\}'` finds no other status discrimination on this path.

**2. Deterministic live reproduction (Playwright, live URL, live bundle).**
`/tmp/.../scratchpad/atk/skeptic2/probe.mjs` — fulfilling POST `/api/v1/session` with each status on the live page:

| status | `#agErr` textContent | `#agSpine` | `#appRoot[inert]` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 401 | `unauthenticated — check the operator name and token` | err | true |
| 404 | `unauthenticated — check the operator name and token` | err | true |
| 500 | `unauthenticated — check the operator name and token` | err | true |
| 502 | `unauthenticated — check the operator name and token` | err | true |
| 503 | `unauthenticated — check the operator name and token` | err | true |
| 429 | `rate limited — wait a minute and retry` | err | true |

Screenshots `/tmp/.../scratchpad/atk/skeptic2/sk_login_{401,404,500,502,503,429}.png`.

**3. The strongest attempted refutation — "maybe some OTHER on-screen signal discriminates" — fails.** `probe2.mjs` captured full `document.body.innerText` for 401 vs 503: **byte-identical** (`identical_401_vs_503: true`), both `Territory Grounder OPERATOR CONSOLE … USERNAME PASSWORD unauthenticated — check the operator name and token Sign in …`. Same `document.title`. The `#agSpine` progress indicator is `aria-hidden="true"` and reads `err` in every failing case, so it discriminates nothing. `#agErr` is the sole channel. Only a transport-level abort (`connectionrefused`) produces a different string (`network error — retry`) — i.e. the honest branch exists but is unreachable for any HTTP-level control-plane failure.

**4. Reproduced with GENUINE server responses, no synthetic fulfill at all** (`probe3.mjs`), which removes the "route interception is not reality" objection:
- Real bad credentials, un-intercepted → network log `401 POST /api/v1/session` → `unauthenticated — check the operator name and token`
- URL rewritten to an unregistered route so the browser receives a real edge/backend 404 → network log `404 POST /api/v1/session-not-registered` → **identical string** (`identical: true`). Screenshots `sk3_realbadcreds401.png`, `sk3_realroute404.png`.

**Mechanism and consequence both check out.** `core/httpapi/router.go:249-251` confirms `if d.Sessions != nil { rt.Handle("/v1/session", …) }` — a 404 on that POST genuinely means the session backend is absent, not a bad password. `core/httpapi/session.go:27-41` shows the handler itself only emits 401/405, so any 5xx/404 necessarily originates outside the credential check. Response headers confirm the topology that makes the consequence bite: `GET /` is served by **openresty straight off disk** (`etag`, `accept-ranges: bytes`, `last-modified`) while `/api/v1/*` is proxied to the Go backend — so during a backend restart the login page renders perfectly and the operator's only feedback is the credential accusation. Incidentally the deployed bundle's `last-modified` of 18:44:11 GMT sits immediately before the claimed 18:54–19:04 GMT (20:54–21:04 CEST) incident window, which corroborates rather than undermines the "deploy/restart" story — though I note I could not independently verify that historical window from logs, and the claim does not depend on it.

**Not excluded by the !736 carve-out.** The authGate modal+inert fix from !736 is already live (I observed `role="dialog" aria-modal="true"` in the served markup and `#appRoot[inert] === true` in every probe) — yet the login error copy is still wrong, so this is orthogonal to all five !736 items. The fix for *this* defect exists only as **uncommitted working-tree changes** on branch `fix/console-login-error-names-the-real-cause`: `git status` shows ` M deploy/console/v2/index.html`, ` M deploy/console/v2/modules/_live/js.txt`, `?? deploy/console/v2/e2e/login-error-honesty.mjs` (the oracle is untracked — `git log` on it returns nothing). Not merged, not deployed.

**No pre-existing oracle catches it.** Of the tracked oracles referencing the login gate, `boot-resilience.mjs` only stubs `/v1/sessions` (the plural read), and `session-boundary.mjs` only asserts the `#api` Access-column label for `/v1/session` (`operator-login`) — neither exercises the POST failure copy. `detail-error-copy.mjs` applies precisely this "a 404 must not tell an operator to sign in again" lens, but only to the detail *read* surface (`/v1/sessions/{ref}`), never to the login POST. The claim's coverage argument is accurate.

Minor wording note that does not affect the verdict: the gate's own field labels read USERNAME/PASSWORD while the error says "operator name and token", so the misdirection is slightly worse than described — but that is cosmetic relative to the core defect.

Next burst at 44198ms => period 25.0s.
- #estatedepth: A.e2-lrow "■ dc1linkwarden02 LXC" -> BODY at 15.4s, same revealConsole<-liveAdopt stack.
- #actions: DIV.ribbon-row "AUTO start-service nginx.service" -> BODY at 19.1s, same stack.
- #modules: BUTTON.mods-tile "NOTIFIER" -> BODY at 0.5s, next burst 25.2s.
So the cadence is a fixed 25.0s rebuild; time-to-loss is phase-dependent (0.5s–19.2s observed), consistent with the claimed "every ~10–25 seconds".

COST (s8_cost.mjs): 34 Tab presses from <body> to reach the first run row on #workflows. At t=20s with no input the previously focused node reported isConnected=false (destroyed, not merely blurred) and .wf-list scrollTop went 400 -> 0. The scroll reset is an extra consequence the reporter did not even claim.

ROOT CAUSE IS PRESENT IN main, NOT FIXED-BUT-UNDEPLOYED: deploy/console/v2/index.html:3080 route() does `view.innerHTML=""; view.append(views[name]())` with no focus save/restore, plus `view.scrollTop=0` at :3093; revealConsole() at :10747 unconditionally calls route() at :10758; liveAdopt() calls revealConsole() at :7901 every poll cycle. LIVE RENDER (kyriakosp, 1600x1000, 2026-07-29; script <scratchpad>, screenshot .../atk/rg1_grounding.png): .grnd-hero-title = "The map met the territory 68.4% of the time"; .grnd-hero-figs = "68.4% / VERIFIER MATCH-RATE / 67 match · 7 partial · 24 deviation"; prose "computed from 98 verdicts and 321 scored predictions, never asserted"; donut "98 TOTAL / match 67 / partial 7 / deviation 24"; first .grnd-foot = "A deviation is the safety-critical case … the action is clamped to never-auto — it can never run unattended again without human sign-off."; rail badge a.navi[data-view=grounding] = "Grounding | 68%". LIVE #actions (.../atk/rg2.mjs, screenshot .../atk/rg2_actions.png): "PREDICTION (MAP) VS OUTCOME (TERRITORY) / 50 of 113 · 52 verified · 1 deviation". The 1-vs-24 contradiction is present on one console.

DB (read-only, live TG postgres): pooled action_verdict = deviation 24 / match 67 / partial 7 (98 rows, 98 distinct action_ids). The project's own documented executed-only anti-join (EXISTS interceptor_gate_verdict g WHERE g.gate='execute' AND g.verdict='pass') gives match 46 / partial 3 / deviation 1 = 50 verdicts, 46/50 = 92.0%; the 48 excluded rows are match 21 / partial 4 / deviation 23. Second independent discriminator: action_execution holds 408 rows over only 43 distinct action_ids; 55 of the 98 verdicts have no execution row and 23 of the 24 deviations have none; restricting by execution rows gives match 40 / partial 2 / deviation 1 — the same answer. The anti-join does not under-count: count(distinct e.action_id) from action_execution lacking a gate execute/pass row = 0. Robust to windowing: within 7 days executed-only is 42/2/1 (93.3%) vs pooled 48/5/20. prediction_verdict = 20 rows, 19 deviation / 1 match, and grep of core/httpapi plus router.go shows no read route, so the separated world-model number is unreachable from the console.

NOT FIXED-BUT-UNDEPLOYED: git log -- core/db/grounding_read.go shows one commit (235f3d8) and main still has the bare `SELECT verdict::text, count(*) FROM action_verdict GROUP BY 1`, while core/db/axis_read.go:556-578 documents that pooling "produced a rate describing neither" and that 23 of 24 deviations were propose-path. NOT COVERED BY THE EXISTING ORACLE: deploy/console/v2/e2e/surface-contradictions.mjs check #3 is the only #grounding assertion and it only compares the falsifiability headline to its own bars, using a synthetic liveState.grounding the test supplies; it never inspects which population the verdicts came from, so it passes regardless.

The consequence follows: the only glanceable accuracy figure understates executed match-rate by 23.6 points (68.4% vs 92.0%) and overstates the safety-critical deviation count 24-fold, with nothing on the surface telling the operator which population it describes.

API: GET /api/v1/grounding -> floor_holds 935, bands {AUTO:521, AUTO_NOTICE:102, POLL_PAUSE:935}. floor_holds is byte-identical to the band count (cmd/grounder/deps.go:281 `FloorHolds: agg.Bands["POLL_PAUSE"]`, still at HEAD).

SAME POPULATION FROM THE SPINE: I re-derived the API's exact query (core/db/grounding_read.go:59-61, DISTINCT ON (external_ref) band FROM session_risk_audit ORDER BY external_ref, created_at DESC) and ran it read-only against live postgres. Bands matched the API exactly. Decomposition by signals_json->>'poll_reason' over the 935: actor-attribution-escalate 394, op-class-not-graduated 173, ood-novel-incident 168, actor-attributed-authorized 77, server-derived-destructive-op 70, irreversible-or-never-auto-floor 27, canary-policy-pinned 14, jailbreak-detected 10, no-committed-prediction 2 — sums to exactly 935. Real floor = 27/935 = 2.9%.

MY STRONGEST REFUTATION ATTEMPT FAILED. I hypothesised poll_reason is a precedence-chosen single label, so an 'op-class-not-graduated' row might ALSO be on the floor (making 935 defensible). core/risk/classifier.go refutes that in the opposite direction: the floor is Step 1 (line 38) and the code comments state the canary/attribution/ungraduated branches run "AFTER the inviolable mechanical floors above (which record the more fundamental poll_reason when they also apply)". A row labelled op-class-not-graduated or canary-policy-pinned therefore PROVABLY failed the floor test. The 187 are not floor holds.

FLOOR IS GENUINELY NARROW AND GENUINELY NON-CONFIGURABLE: core/safety/safety.go:67 neverAutoFloor is a 30-slug unexported map (mkfs, dropdb, reboot, kubectl-delete, ...). So the sentence's second clause is true about the floor and false about the 935 it is attached to. The console contradicts itself: live #governance INVARIANT reads "Irreversible ops · security devices · data destruction · full-cluster scope can never reach AUTO" and reports the band neutrally as "521 auto · 102 notice · 935 pause".

CONSEQUENCE VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED: I swept all 22 live views (sk_floor_2.mjs) for any rendering of poll_reason / op-class-not-graduated / attribution-escalate / canary-policy-pinned — ZERO hits on every view. WHAT I DID (independent, live, signed in via LDAP against https://territory-grounder.example.net/, read-only — no KILL, no approve/deny, no form submit, no vote). Scripts: <scratchpad>, m2.mjs, m3.mjs. I measured #breaker geometry at 16 widths, then walked the .sw text node character-by-character with DOM Ranges and computed each glyph's VISIBLE width against the breaker's clip edge (bb.left + borderLeft + clientWidth), and took rendered crops of both states (state B produced by writing the text node + data-mode only, then restoring — no app setter, no network).

WHAT REPRODUCED. The clip is genuine: #breaker scrollWidth 262-270 vs clientWidth 139@1024, 158@1080, 185@1152, 224@1280, 249@1366, full only at >=1400-1424. Live posture is operational, .sw colour rgb(155,82,14).

WHY THE CLAIM FAILS — three independent breaks.

1) SCOPE IS WRONG. "Below ~1080px ... clipped to a single glyph ... identical visible string" does not hold at 1080 or 1040. Measured visible glyph widths (px of 7.8px monospace cells): 1080 ON = "O:7.8 n:7.8 :7.8 ·:7.8" / OFF = "O:7.8 f:7.8 f:7.8 :5.9" — crops z_on_1080.png / z_off_1080.png read plainly "MUTATION [toggle] ON ·" vs "MUTATION [toggle] OFF". 1040 ON = "ON " / OFF = "OF" (z_on_1040.png / z_off_1040.png). The text-only ambiguity band is roughly 1000-1036 CSS px (~36px wide), not "<=1080, degraded from 1424 downward"; and at <=820px the max-width:820 rule hides .annun/.who/.clock and the FULL string returns ("On · Operational" all 16 glyphs at 810 and 760).

2) "COLOUR-ONLY" IS FALSE — the load-bearing sentence. At 1024 the .nub is FULLY inside the clip box (nub right edge 283 vs clip edge 301.1) and it is a two-position switch: [data-mode="operational"] .nub::after has transform matrix(1,0,0,1,11,0), read-only has none. Pixel-measured from my own crops (atk/skb/on_1024.png, off_1024.png), the knob dot occupies x 112-120 in ON and x 101-109 in OFF — centroid 115.9 vs 105.0, a 10.9px displacement of a 9px dot, i.e. the two positions do not overlap at all. The 5x zooms z_on_1024.png / z_off_1024.png show it unmistakably: amber knob hard right vs green knob hard left. The claimant's own offered evidence (atk/amb_on_1024.png, atk/amb_off_1024.png) shows exactly the same thing. So the distinction survives as a canonical toggle affordance, not "a colour and an 11px nub offset" reduced to nothing.

3) THE STRING DESCRIPTION IS WRONG. No ellipsis renders anywhere — text-overflow:ellipsis on .breaker is inert because .breaker is display:inline-flex (index.html:169) with no directly-contained inline text, so it is a hard clip, never "O…". And the two states are not glyph-identical even at 1024: ON renders "O" plus 2.4-3.4px of the following "n"; OFF renders only "O" (7.1-7.8px). The crops differ in element width too (142px ON vs 140px OFF).

CONSEQUENCE DOES NOT FOLLOW. The header at 1024 reads: literal label "MUTATION", separator, a two-position switch with the knob at opposite ends of a 24px track, in amber vs green. An operator is not left with colour alone, so "cannot tell whether the estate is actuable or read-only" is not supported by the evidence offered.

NOT A !736 ARTEFACT — this is unrelated to the UTC columns / authGate inert / SSE-on-signout / #api Access / disabled-estate-controls set.

ADJACENT HONEST NOTE (not asserted as a finding, offered because it is a different shape from the claim): in the ~821-1000px band the clip is far worse than the claim describes — at 960px clientWidth is 113 and ZERO .sw glyphs are visible with the nub's right edge also past the clip edge, so only "MUTATION" survives; that band is below the standard-laptop range and I did not develop it into a consequence.

Drawer only: #appRoot[inert]=true and CDP AX for .kill = {ignored:true, reasons:['inertElement']}. result.why:
I could not refute it — it reproduced independently, exactly as stated, on the live console (https://territory-grounder.example.net/, LDAP login, headless Chromium + CDP AX). My own scripts, not the reporter's: <scratchpad>, .../skv_control.mjs, .../skv_c4.mjs.

MEASURED (skv_inert.mjs, viewport 1440x900, #actions -> first .ribbon-row of 50 -> Ctrl+K -> Escape):
- A drawer only: {appInert:true, drawerOpen:true, drawerRole:"dialog", drawerAriaModal:"true"}; CDP Accessibility.getPartialAXTree on .kill = {ignored:true, ignoredReasons:["inertElement"], role:"none"}. Screenshot .../atk/skv_A_drawer.png.
- B drawer+palette: {appInert:true, palOpen:true}; .kill still {ignored:true, reasons:["inertElement"]}.
- C after Escape: {appInert:false, drawerOpen:true, drawerAriaModal:"true", drawerRole:"dialog", drawerInert:false, palOpen:false, palInert:true}; .kill = {ignored:false, reasons:[], role:"button", name:"KILL"}; .navi[data-view=ledger] = {ignored:false, name:"Ledger"}; #appRoot unignored; getFullAXTree = 1579 unignored named nodes; 83 focusable elements outside both overlays. Screenshot .../atk/skv_C_after_escape.png. Numbers match the reporter's to the element (83 focusables, same AX verdicts).
- Blast radius as claimed: 14 consecutive Tabs all stayed inside #drawer; document.elementFromPoint over the Ledger nav returns #scrim, and Playwright's own real click on .navi[data-view=actions] timed out 30s with "<div id="scrim" class="scrim open"> intercepts pointer events". So the leak is accessibility-tree-only, as the reporter conservatively stated.

CONTROLS I ran to try to break it (skv_control.mjs):
- Drawer alone, idle: appInert stayed true at t+4s and t+12s — so the inert removal is caused by the nested open/close, not by an SSE tick or re-render.
- After the nested leak, appInert was still false 12s later — it is never restored; the operator's whole remaining session in that drawer is in the leaked state.
- inert is not restored by anything short of a reload/next overlay.

NOT one of the !736 items (UTC columns, authGate modal+inert, sign-out closes SSE, #api Access column, disabled estate controls). Still unfixed at current HEAD (f1dd372): deploy/console/v2/index.html overlayClose does `if (o.inerted) o.inerted.removeAttribute('inert');` with no depth check, and each overlayOpen stores inerted=#appRoot. The oracle that should catch it, deploy/console/v2/e2e/overlay-semantics.mjs, asserts the opposite for the single-overlay case ("palette: the page is reachable again", !appInert after close) and never opens two overlays — so a green suite is guaranteed here.

CONSEQUENCE — holds, with one honest caveat: the state is genuinely self-contradictory (drawer role=dialog aria-modal=true while #appRoot and every control behind it, including KILL, are back in the AX tree), and the console's own design comment says the page behind a modal "must be unreachable, not merely covered". Caveat for the parent: screen readers that honour aria-modal (NVDA/JAWS/VoiceOver browse mode) would still confine the virtual buffer to the dialog subtree, so the practical severity for those AT users is lower than "is offered the entire console" implies; the defect is best stated as "the inert defense the console relies on is silently dropped while the modal is still up, leaving announced modality and actual tree membership disagreeing". I also checked whether the leak is worse than claimed (AT-style activation): element.click() on the Ledger nav changed location.hash to #ledger BOTH before and after the leak (i.e. while #appRoot was still inert), so programmatic dispatch is not a valid AT proxy and gives no basis to escalate beyond the reporter's bounded claim.

ADJACENT FINDING my control turned up, which the parent should know because it is a superset of this bug and is NOT nesting-specific: with only the drawer open, a single Escape gives {appInert:false, drawerOpen:true, drawerAriaModal:"true", scrimOpen:true} — Escape pops the overlay (setting inert+aria-hidden on the drawer itself) but never calls closeDrawer(), so the drawer stays visible with #scrim still intercepting every pointer event. That is what killed skv_control.mjs mid-run: the subsequent real click on .navi[data-view="actions"] failed for 30s against "scrim open intercepts pointer events". So the mechanism label "no reference counting" is accurate for the reported path but incomplete as a root cause: the drawer's overlay entry has no onClose, and Escape on the drawer alone wedges the console (visible-but-inert drawer, no visible way out) until reload.

findings.evidence: MECHANISM, in the DEPLOYED bundle (fetched live from /index.html, 902,476 bytes, saved to <scratchpad>): `routeFocusKey()` present=true; its last-resort identity `const peers=Array.from((view||document).querySelectorAll(tag)); const i=peers.indexOf(a); return {sel:tag, nth:i}` present=true (string `peers.indexOf(a)` found). AX (CDP getFullAXTree, #command): 17 nodes role=button name="Approve" and 17 role=button name="Deny" — 34 controls, 2 distinct names, zero descriptions, and every `.appr-row`/`.wrapcard` ancestor is `ignored: uninteresting` so there is no group boundary either. PROOF RUN (atk/ax/18_ordinal.mjs): live queue = 16 decisions, order printed. Focused the Approve of row 4 → BEFORE: {ordinalAmongViewButtons: 8, ref: "librenms-dc1-181407", action: "start start-guest on dc1wallos01", nRows: 16, announce: ""}. One decision was then removed from the real /v1/decisions payload via Playwright route interception (client-side only — this simulates another operator answering the oldest item; the queue also shrank organically 17→16 rows during this same session, and the list is ordered oldest-first so eviction always happens at the top). findings.evidence: atk/ax/15_lb.mjs + atk/ax/19_lb2.mjs. Census: role=listbox aria-label="Governed runs", listbox tabIndex=-1, aria-activedescendant=null, 50 role=option children, distinct option tabIndex values = [0] (all 50 in the tab order), option ids = none, exactly 1 aria-selected=true. AX (CDP getFullAXTree): 50 role=option nodes, 50 unique names, e.g. "librenms-dc1-182069 Service-up/down dc1ghostfolio01 ✓ MATCH 0s AUTO". Keyboard, with option[0] focused: ArrowDown → {scrollTop: 0→40, docScroll: 0, focIdx: 0, selIdx: 0, ad: null}; ArrowDown again → scrollTop 80, focIdx 0, selIdx 0; End → scrollTop 1834, focIdx 0, selIdx 0, ad still null. So after End the focused option is 1834px above the visible area of its own scroll container while retaining focus. Tab traversal measured: 49 consecutive tab stops after option[0] are themselves options. deploy/console/v2/e2e/workflows-focus.mjs contains zero references to Arrow keys or aria-activedescendant (grep for 'Arrow|activedescendant' → no matches); it tests key stability and announcement only.
findings.consequence: NVDA/JAWS/VoiceOver switch to focus mode inside role=listbox and hand the arrow keys to the widget, so an assistive-tech operator on the workflows triage index can neither arrow through the 50 governed runs (the pattern the role promises) nor read by arrow — the only traversal is 50 Tab presses, and one End press leaves the focus indicator scrolled 1834px off-screen.

findings.claim: Navigating with the command palette — one of the three routes the register credits for 2.4.5 — leaves document.activeElement on <body> and announces nothing, unlike every other navigation path in the console.
findings.where: LIVE https://territory-grounder.example.net/ · Ctrl+K palette (`#palScrim` role=dialog aria-modal, `#palInput` role=combobox, `#palRes` role=listbox "Palette results") · measured from #command → #ledger
findings.evidence: atk/ax/11_pal.mjs, atk/ax/12_pal2.mjs, atk/ax/14_final.mjs. Palette semantics are otherwise correct: aria-activedescendant walks palopt0→palopt4 on ArrowDown and back on ArrowUp; AX names are clean ("▸ Ledger tamper-evident, hash-chained, actor-typed view"); #appRoot gains inert on open; Escape restores focus to the exact prior control (measured: prior focus = `BUTTON.btn primary "Approve"`, after Escape = same button). But Enter on a result → hash="#ledger", `document.activeElement` = BODY, `#tgAnnounce`.textContent = "" (empty). Next Tab lands on `A.skip-link "Skip to main content"` (tab index 0 of the document); the Tab after that is `#breaker`. For comparison, activating a rail item with Enter keeps focus on the link (`{tag:'A', cls:'navi on', txt:'Alerts 2076'}`) and the skip link correctly moves focus to `DIV#view[tabindex=-1]`, so the console already owns a landing target. Cost of the reset measured on #command: 33 Tab presses from the document start to the first Approve button. Cause, in the deployed bundle: `execPal(it){closePal(false); ... route(it.id);}` — the restore path is deliberately skipped and nothing replaces it.
findings.consequence: An assistive-tech operator gets no confirmation that the jump happened at all and their reading cursor is reset to the top of the document, so the console's global jump affordance costs them the position they were holding on every use.

(a) The mutation-posture flip and the \"Posture unverified\" state: #breaker is a <button> whose accessible name IS the state (\"MUTATION ON · OPERATIONAL\") and setBreaker() re-runs every ~5s but is in no live region, so a posture change would be announced to nobody — I could not provoke a real flip read-only, and CDP Network.emulateNetworkConditions offline did NOT disturb the already-open EventSource (connTxt stayed \"SSE LIVE\" and posture events kept arriving for 45s), so the \"API · STREAM DOWN\" path stayed unreachable. Unverified, not reported. (b) The organic version of finding 1: I observed the queue shrink 17→16 rows on its own during the session but did not happen to be holding focus at that instant, so the retarget itself was triggered by dropping one item from the real /v1/decisions payload client-side. The mechanism, the payload and the 25s refresh are all live and deployed; only the timing was made deterministic, and I state that in the finding. (c) I did NOT click KILL, approve/deny anything, submit the seal form, or vote. CONFIRMED, number for number:
- Before #menuBtn: #rail transform matrix(1,0,0,1,-230,0), rect x=-230. After click: class "rail open", transform matrix(1,0,0,1,0,0), rect x=0 y=52 w=230 h=792.
- .scrim: className stays exactly "scrim" (it never gains .open — only openDrawer() does that), computed pointerEvents="none", opacity="0", zIndex="40", display="block", rect 0,0,390x844. So it is inert decoration, as claimed.
- Dismissal attempts, each +500ms then re-read of #rail.classList.contains('open'): scrim.click() -> true; mouse(350,600) -> true; mouse(340,400) -> true; mouse(300,700) -> true; Escape -> true. Second session: mouse(320,500) -> true. Keyboard variants I added that the reporter did not test: Escape with focus ON #menuBtn -> still open; Escape with focus INSIDE the rail (a.navi[data-view=command]) -> still open; 8 Tabs stay inside the rail and it stays open. Only #menuBtn re-click, or a route(), closes it.
- No inertness: document.body[inert]=false, #view[inert]=false, #view aria-hidden=null. Screenshot shows the background at full brightness, undimmed.
- Exposed-strip enumeration (my own, over a[href],button,[role=button],input,select,textarea,[tabindex]): 4 hit-testable controls with centre x>230 — API contract (258,26), account (293,26), KILL (347,26), all three in the always-exposed header above the rail's top edge y=52 — and in the region the rail actually covers vertically, exactly ONE: BUTTON.facet "Auto", rect x=250 y=88 w=50 h=24, centre (275,100), elementFromPoint resolves to itself. Same single element the reporter got.

CONSEQUENCE — I pushed further and it survives, on LIVE data. I tapped (275,100) with the rail open (a client-side filter, no actuation, within the read-only constraint). Result: facet aria-pressed flipped All=true->Auto=true, #view.scrollHeight 6841->4953, and the live triage table caption changed from "showing 50 of 1560 recorded" to "showing 13 of 50 fetched (1560 recorded) · filter: auto". The rows that vanished are real: librenms-dc1-182072, 182065, 182046/47, tg-liveness-dc1cloudbeaver01-1785359520, ... 37 live pending sessions dated 2026-07-29 19:10–21:31 dropped out. Approve/Deny button count stayed 32, so the live pending-approvals block above is unaffected — but 37 of 50 live triage rows are. And the facets bar is sticky: after scrolling #view to scrollTop=1869 the Auto chip is still at (275,100) and still hit-testable, so the hazard band is permanent, not scroll-dependent.

NOT one of the !736 fixes (UTC columns, authGate modal+inert, sign-out/SSE, #api Access, disabled estate controls) — and repo HEAD, which is ahead of the deployed image, still has only `$("#menuBtn").addEventListener("click",()=>$("#rail").classList.toggle("open"))` with no scrim activation and a global Escape handler that calls closeDrawer()/closePal() only. Not fixed-but-undeployed. And no oracle covers it: `grep -c menuBtn deploy/console/v2/e2e/*.mjs` = 0 across all 44 files; "rail" appears only in badge/enumeration contexts; overlay-semantics.mjs and drawer-unwedgeable.mjs never touch #rail.

TWO WORDING CORRECTIONS the reporter should fix (neither changes the verdict):
1. "activate a live filter control UNDERNEATH" is wrong — the Auto chip is not under the rail, it is in the 160px strip beside it (rail spans x 0–230; chip x 250–300). The right frame is the missing inert/scrim, not z-order leakage.
2. "the tap intended to close the menu INSTEAD reaches..." is wrong, and the truth is worse: route() runs `if(innerWidth<=820)$("#rail").classList.remove("open")`, so tapping that chip DOES close the rail. The operator gets exactly the feedback they wanted (menu closed) while the live triage list silently drops from 50 rows to 13 — disclosed only by a 10px caption and a chip highlight.
One honest limit on severity, which I would state alongside the finding: the actionable target is 50x24 = 1200px^2 of a 160x792 = 126,720px^2 exposed strip (~0.9%), and it sits 36px below the header, not where a mid-screen reflex tap lands — my four mid-content tap points all hit non-interactive text (P.desc "[POLL_PAUSE] Device-Down on dc1meali", DIVs) and did nothing at all except fail to close the rail. So the reliable defect is "the rail is undismissable by both standard gestures and by Escape, with a fully live background"; the filter-flip is the real but lower-probability tail of it.

Nothing establishes what a non-admin or non-trace-read operator sees, or whether the console offers controls that will 403 for them. ### 2. Is the register's claim defensible?

**No.** Four specific reasons, in descending order of how badly "covered" overstates "verified".

**(a) The register contradicts itself inside one file.** Line 24: `WCAG 2.2 A+AA rows: 51 — covered 37, **UNCOVERED 15**`. Line 102: `**2026-07-29 — THIS LIST IS NOW EMPTY.**`. Both are present in `docs/CONSOLE-UX-AUDIT-REGISTER.md` right now. Whichever a reader quotes, the other is there to contradict them — and the memory index quotes the *empty* one as settled fact.

**(b) "Scope is closed" sits directly above eleven CONFIRMED, OPEN, live defects.** §S7 lists S7-4 … S7-14 as "CONFIRMED and still OPEN", and §S6 ends "**The register's scope is now closed.**" I confirmed four of those eleven are still in the bytes being served right now. A register in which "covered" coexists with a dozen known-live defects is tracking *audit activity*, not *console state*. That is the single largest overstatement, because the word most readers take from it is "verified".

**(c) The rows with the highest claimed coverage point at oracles that cannot see the console.** See Q3 — this is the load-bearing part.

**(d) The pass-rate on the 15 previously-UNCOVERED rows is not a discovery rate.** §S6 closed them 13 PASS / 1 confirmed / 1 refuted in a single workflow. The register's own lifetime rate is 66 confirmed / 25 refuted. Fifteen never-examined criteria yielding one defect is what a *checklist walk* produces, not what an audit produces — and one of the two non-PASS rows is 3.3.4, closed as refuted without exercising the control.

### 3. Oracles that could not fail on a real defect

There are **43** oracle files, not 19 (`ls *.mjs | grep -v serve.mjs | wc -l` = 43; `run.sh` derives the list from the directory, so all 43 execute). The structural problem is shared by all of them:

**Every oracle grades a local static copy with no backend.** `run.sh` starts `serve.mjs` on 127.0.0.1 and exports `CONSOLE_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:$PORT`; `serve.mjs` 404s anything not on disk, so `/api/**` is 404. CI's `console-e2e` job runs `bash run.sh` and nothing else. `grep -l territory-grounder deploy/console/v2/e2e/*.mjs` returns exactly one file — and the hit is a *comment* on line 3 of `console-foundations.mjs`. `grep -rn "CONSOLE_BASE=https"` over the whole repo: **zero hits**. **No oracle has ever run against the deployed console.**

I measured what that harness actually presents (`local.mjs`, served from `deploy/console/v2` on port 8321): exactly **one** API call happens for the whole page life — `GET /api/v1/whoami → 404` — and then `#appRoot` is `hidden=true` **and** `inert=true`, `#view` innerText is **0 characters**, `#annun` reads `"AUTO — NOTICE — PAUSE —"`, `#breaker` reads `"Mutation Off · Read-only"`, `.who` reads `"—"`, `#connTxt` reads `"SSE CLOSED"`.

**16 of 43 oracles install no `page.route`/`context.route` at all.** Twelve of those reveal the app themselves with `setGate(false)` and therefore grade the placeholder console; four never reveal it. I ran eight of them against that harness — **all eight exit 0**:

- **`kill-reachable.mjs` — cannot fail on the defect it was written for, and says so in its own header:** *"its mutation control (revert `.breaker` to `flex:0 0 auto`) came back GREEN, so this file does NOT reproduce the overflow… A defect that only exists when real data widens the row cannot be caught by a harness that has no real data. So the load-bearing assertion for THIS defect lives in the live e2e."* **There is no live e2e.** It printed `ok @1920: KILL is fully within the viewport` and passed. On live at 1440 the header's elastic chips carry `"Mutation On · Operational"`, `"AUTO 524 / NOTICE 102 / PAUSE 941"` and the operator name — the exact content that produced the original 1499px defect, and the exact content this oracle never sees.
- **`console-foundations.mjs` — prints its own vacuity and still returns green:** `SKIP 0 cells rendered (unauthenticated) — asserted NOTHING; proof is the live run`, then `console-foundations: all checks passed`, exit 0. The CI log line a human reads is the green one.
- **`contrast-tokens.mjs` — cited by the register for 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum), "both themes, all 22 views + tints".** It enumerates CSS **rules** out of `document.styleSheets` and synthesises elements by adding class names (`el.classList.add(...)` at line 161), on a page whose `#view` is empty. It never measures rendered ink in a rendered view. It cannot see a hard-coded inline colour, a token overridden at a deeper cascade level, or any text that only exists when real data renders — which is exactly the failure mode this project already recorded ("a literal ink cannot follow a token; a rendered scan is a SAMPLE"). It reported `dark: 15 ink tokens (worst 4.59:1) · 55 text chips` and passed.
- **`table-semantics.mjs` — cited for 1.3.1 Info and Relationships / "151 header cells with no scope, 38 tables".** It builds its own DOM (`document.createElement('div')` at lines 41 and 59) and unit-tests `nameTables()`. It visits none of the console's real tables. Green against an empty `#view`.
- **`keyboard-operability.mjs`, `overlay-semantics.mjs`, `announcements.mjs`, `login-error-honesty.mjs`** — all green against the placeholder console. `keyboard-operability` reported `ok ENTER selects a run` on a `#workflows` that has no runs from a 404 `/v1/sessions`; `announcements` reported `ok the seal form carries its own live region` without a live secrets read.

**Eight oracles explicitly defer their load-bearing assertion to a "live" run that does not exist as code:** `login-error-honesty`, `console-foundations`, `deeplink-every-view`, `contrast-tokens`, `kill-reachable`, `fixture-hostnames`, `session-boundary`, `ledger-never-fabricates`. That honesty is genuinely good practice — and it is a dangling reference in all eight cases.

**And nothing asserts deployment identity.** `run.sh`'s only integrity check is `served bytes == on-disk bytes` — self-consistency, never repo-vs-production. The post-deploy gate `scripts/verify-deploy.sh` (48 lines) asserts only that `/` returns 200 and `/api/v1/whoami` returns 401. So the suite can be green on `main` while a different artifact serves, and the four-way md5 churn during this fan-out means **findings and refutations produced by different lenses are not provably about the same file**. That is a register-level gap with no row.

The corollary for the current 16 findings: the register's §S7 built `overlay-nesting-and-actuation-focus.mjs` with four mutation controls PROVEN RED — that is the best oracle in the directory and the right pattern. It still runs only against the local copy with a stubbed API, so it locks the *code shape* of the fix, not the deployed behaviour.

### 4. Blunt percentage

**~60% of this console's UX is verified end-to-end. Roughly 35% is regression-locked** (i.e. a fresh regression would turn something red without a human running an ad-hoc agent).

Basis — weighted by how much of an operator's actual decision surface each slice is:

| slice | weight | verified | contribution |
|---|---|---|---|
| read path · desktop · Chromium · healthy backend | 0.40 | 0.85 — 22 views and 29 endpoints genuinely enumerated and hammered by ~90 agents | 0.34 |
| degraded-backend / failure states | 0.15 | 0.75 — per-endpoint 500 + total starvation + hang, honestly done; SSE lanes and 403-vs-500 divergence untouched | 0.11 |
| small viewport / zoom / both themes | 0.10 | 0.70 — I closed 320px and dark-theme geometry; RTL, forced-colors and 400% *text-only* remain proxy-verified | 0.07 |
| accessibility / AT | 0.10 | 0.50 — a real AX-tree census exists; no real screen reader, and the flagship contrast oracle measures tokens not ink | 0.05 |
| **write path** (approve, deny, KILL, seal, elevate, toggle) | **0.15** | **0.05** | **0.01** |
| multi-operator · long-horizon · data extremes · non-UTC · non-Chromium | 0.10 | 0.15 — Firefox now cleared; the rest at zero | 0.015 |
| **total** | | | **≈0.60** |

The 35% regression-locked figure is the same table restricted to what an automated oracle catches: divide the first row by roughly two (no live target, no real data for 16 of 43 files, four oracles that grade a hidden page), and set the write-path and multi-operator rows to zero.

**What specifically remains, in the order I would spend the next effort:**

1. **A live oracle.** One harness that signs in against `$TG_CONSOLE_URL` with a CI operator credential and re-runs the widest existing oracles with real data. Eight oracle files already name this thing as the home of their load-bearing assertion. It does not exist. Until it does, the register's WCAG rows for contrast, keyboard, tables and KILL-reachability are claims about a placeholder page.
2. **Deployment identity in the gate.** `verify-deploy.sh` should assert the served `index.html` hash equals the built artifact's, and every audit finding should record that hash. Cheap, and it retroactively makes the register's 66 findings citable.
3. **The write path.** It is 15% of the surface, ~0% verified, and it is the only part that changes real infrastructure. It needs a staging control plane where Approve can actually be pressed — no read-only lens will ever reach it, and closing 3.3.4 by arguing about reachability was the wrong call.
4. **Fix the eight still-live findings** (S7-4/5/6/7/10/12/13/14) rather than re-confirming them; three separate lenses re-derived them today at full cost.
5. **Add the missing rows to the register before auditing them**: WRITE-PATH, AUTHZ-DIFFERENTIATED-UX, CONCURRENT-OPERATORS, ENGINE-MATRIX, DEPLOY-IDENTITY, LONG-HORIZON, DATA-EXTREMES, CLIENT-ENVIRONMENT. Those eight rows are why a fan-out of six lenses returned 25% novelty: the enumeration is complete against WCAG and incomplete against this console.
